name: 03-ten-polyps-mixed
description: Maximum of ten specimens (A-J) across all six polyp types and all sites. DELIBERATE EDIT 2026-09-22: printed text respelled to British on request. This breaks spelling parity with the Phase 0 legacy HTML app, which still prints "Cecum"; every other byte is unchanged. Do not regenerate with capture-fixtures - it drives the legacy app and would revert this. Diagnosis connector lower-cased deliberately on 2026-09-24 ("TUBULAR ADENOMA with LOW GRADE DYSPLASIA", the released house form) at the user's request, so each capitalised term codes separately in SNOMED; the legacy app printed "WITH".

expected.report:
SPECIMEN:
(A) Caecum polyp
(B) Ascending colon polyp
(C) Hepatic flexure polyp
(D) Transverse colon polyp
(E) Splenic flexure polyp
(F) Descending colon polyp
(G) Sigmoid polyp
(H) Rectosigmoid polyp
(I) Rectum polyp
(J) Colon polyp

MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION:
(A)  Sections show a polypoid piece of large intestinal mucosa featuring tubular crypts with low grade dysplasia. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(B)  Sections show a serrated polyp with architectural features in keeping with a sessile serrated lesion / adenoma. No cytological dysplasia is identified. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(C)  Sections show a polypoid piece of large intestinal mucosa featuring hyperplastic crypts with stellate-shaped lumina, in keeping with hyperplastic polyp. There is no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy.

(D)  Sections show a polypoid fragment of large intestinal mucosa with tubulovillous architecture and low grade dysplasia. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(E)  Sections show a polypoid piece of large intestinal mucosa featuring tubular crypts with high grade dysplasia. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(F)  Sections show a serrated polyp with ectopic crypt formation and conventional low grade dysplasia, in keeping with a traditional serrated adenoma. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(G)  Sections show a polypoid fragment of large intestinal mucosa with predominant villous architecture and high grade dysplasia. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(H)  Sections show a sessile serrated lesion / adenoma with superimposed low grade dysplasia. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(I)  Sections show a polypoid piece of large intestinal mucosa featuring hyperplastic crypts with stellate-shaped lumina, in keeping with hyperplastic polyp. There is no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy.

(J)  Sections show a polypoid piece of large intestinal mucosa featuring tubular crypts with low grade dysplasia. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

DIAGNOSIS:
(A) CAECUM, Caecum polyp, polypectomy - TUBULAR ADENOMA with LOW GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(B) ASCENDING COLON, Ascending colon polyp, polypectomy - SESSILE SERRATED LESION / ADENOMA.
(C) HEPATIC FLEXURE, Hepatic flexure polyp, polypectomy - HYPERPLASTIC POLYP.
(D) TRANSVERSE COLON, Transverse colon polyp, polypectomy - TUBULOVILLOUS ADENOMA with LOW GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(E) SPLENIC FLEXURE, Splenic flexure polyp, polypectomy - TUBULAR ADENOMA with HIGH GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(F) DESCENDING COLON, Descending colon polyp, polypectomy - TRADITIONAL SERRATED ADENOMA with LOW GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(G) SIGMOID, Sigmoid polyp, polypectomy - VILLOUS ADENOMA with HIGH GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(H) RECTOSIGMOID, Rectosigmoid polyp, polypectomy - SESSILE SERRATED LESION / ADENOMA with LOW GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(I) RECTUM, Rectum polyp, polypectomy - HYPERPLASTIC POLYP.
(J) COLON, Colon polyp, polypectomy - TUBULAR ADENOMA with LOW GRADE DYSPLASIA.
